skill.name: building-mcp-servers
skill.description: Guides developers through secure Model Context Protocol server integration for Claude Code plugins, including server type selection, authentication, configuration files, validation, and testing.
skill.summary: Build secure MCP server integrations for Claude Code plugins.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder URLs, placeholder environment variables, and defensive validation logic. One semantic risk remains: the documentation includes an unpinned npx-based MCP server example that could create supply-chain exposure if copied into production. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions or advise users to install and review dependencies before enabling stdio MCP servers.
State that users must replace example endpoints and verify remote MCP server ownership before enabling them.
Label command examples as manual verification steps and warn users not to run them in untrusted plugin directories.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Package Execution Example
semantic_findings.description: The database integration example uses npx -y to run an MCP server package without a version pin. Users who copy it may fetch and execute changing third-party code at runtime.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example configuration directly names npx -y and an npm package without a pinned version. It is documentation rather than automatic execution, so the risk is real but limited.

content.value_statement: MCP setup can expose secrets, weak URLs, or fragile plugin configuration. This skill guides secure server selection, configuration, validation, and documentation for Claude Code plugins.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use stdio, HTTP, SSE, or WebSocket MCP servers.
Provides safe configuration patterns for local and remote MCP integrations.
Documents environment variable usage for API keys, tokens, and database URLs.
Includes a Python validator for MCP configuration structure and security warnings.
Gives testing and debugging steps for Claude Code MCP connections.
limitations: It does not build a complete MCP server implementation from source.
It cannot verify third-party MCP server behavior or package integrity.
Generated configurations still require user-provided credentials and endpoint review.
The validation script checks common issues, not every possible security flaw.

use_cases.title: Add a Hosted API MCP Integration
use_cases.description: Configure a Claude Code plugin to connect to a secure hosted MCP endpoint with documented authentication.

use_cases.title: Validate Plugin MCP Configuration
use_cases.description: Check an MCP configuration for required fields, weak URL schemes, hardcoded secrets, and path portability.

use_cases.title: Document Required Secrets
use_cases.description: Create clear setup notes for environment variables, credential storage, and safe local testing.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Server Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the right MCP server type for a Claude Code plugin that connects to [service]. Ask for any missing requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Secure Config
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an MCP configuration for [service] using [stdio, HTTP, SSE, or WebSocket]. Use environment variables for every secret.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Config
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this MCP configuration for security, portability, and Claude Code compatibility. List required fixes before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Plugin Integration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an end-to-end plan to add MCP support to this plugin, including manifest changes, validation, documentation, and test steps.

output_examples.output: A recommended HTTP MCP setup, required environment variables, HTTPS guidance, and validation steps before publishing.

output: Findings grouped by errors, warnings, and recommendations.
Notes for insecure protocols, hardcoded secrets, and non-portable paths.
A short list of release-blocking fixes.

output_examples.input: Document the secrets needed by my MCP server.
output_examples.output: A concise setup section that names each environment variable and explains how users should store credentials.

best_practices: Use environment variable references for every credential and document each required variable.
Use HTTPS or WSS for remote servers, with localhost exceptions only for development.
Restrict auto-allowed MCP tools to the smallest safe set.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode API keys, bearer tokens, passwords, or database URLs in MCP configuration.
Do not use HTTP or WS for remote MCP services that transmit sensitive data.
Do not enable broad MCP tool access before reviewing tool permissions and side effects.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps configure MCP server integrations for Claude Code plugins and document the required setup.

faq.question: Does it support local MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers stdio servers that run local Node.js, Python, or command-based MCP processes.

faq.question: Does it support remote MCP services?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket patterns with secure URL and authentication guidance.

faq.question: How are secrets handled?
faq.answer: The skill recommends environment variable references and documentation instead of hardcoded credential values.

faq.question: Can it validate my configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a validator script for JSON structure, required fields, URL schemes, paths, and secret patterns.

faq.question: Is third-party MCP server code verified?
faq.answer: No. Users must review external servers, packages, and endpoints before enabling them in a plugin.
